editorialNote: Catalog blurbs are specific to their works when manuscript text or author-provided source summaries are available. Unreviewed entries retain existing copy pending access to the publication itself; do not present unverified descriptions as read manuscripts.

items.title: 35 YO
items.description: A fractured first-person record of isolation, queer self-translation, chemical sleep, and the effort to survive without turning pain into a neat redemption story. These poems preserve unfinished thoughts and emotional loops instead of smoothing them into certainty.

items.title: GRENBK:DTW
items.description: Detroit's queer cultural life, the closing of Spot Lite, Paradise Valley's contested memory, and the first installment of New August share the pages of this inaugural literary review. Criticism, reportage, and fiction refuse the city's tidy official story.

items.title: Palmer Park: GRLS
items.description: A title from the Palmer Park literary cycle.

items.title: Palmer Park: BOIS
items.description: At Palmer Park, Lola, Charles, Manson, Paxton, and Gloria May occupy a stage mapped across a gazebo, pickleball court, and cruising ground. This theatrical outline uses sonnet choruses and shifting character zones to examine queer identity, intimacy, and the park's social boundaries.

items.title: The Winter That Asked for Soup
items.description: When a blizzard swallows Delray, Margot Johannesburg-Mintz keeps her harbor bistro serving soup while an old Hungarian weather tale takes flesh. A wandering scholar, an immense hungry visitor, and Axiom's absurd rules turn one shared meal into an act of civic defiance.

items.title: The Inheritance of Fear — Proposal Pack
items.description: A facilitator's discussion packet examines the fears families and communities pass down as rules. Guided prompts move from gender expectations and protective secrecy to chosen kinship, asking when an instruction offered as care becomes a limit on freedom.

items.title: The Inheritance of Fear
items.description: This guided forum asks what happens when inherited advice about identity, safety, and belonging outlives the danger that shaped it. The discussion treats privacy as a choice rather than a flaw and invites participants to examine what they wish to keep or revise.

items.title: Internment of Solace
items.description: Thirteen-year-old Asa Bell uncovers a buried mechanical listener beneath a former Delray switching yard. As its heart responds to unfinished stories, he confronts a city that would rather classify grief than hear it, and the difference between reviving a witness and claiming ownership.

items.title: Corrosive Solace
items.description: In the aftermath of Delray's flood, Asa Bell and his family repair damaged infrastructure while Axiom moves to reclaim the mechanical listener. The second Solace installment follows a struggle over who may hold the city's memories and the machinery that bears them.

items.title: Commissary of Whimsy
items.description: A girl enters the market beneath Delray, where ghosts, ghouls, wolves, and rival clans trade what the white market has excluded. Commerce becomes a contest over care, value, and who gets to exist outside Axiom's books.

items.title: The Maladaptive Parade of Trauma
items.description: Literary criticism on trauma, interpretation, and the institutions that shape experience.

items.title: Lock & Bolt
items.description: When Asher Aster inexplicably drowns aboard a city bus, cemetery groundskeeper Jay honors his request for burial among flowers. Striking bees, unusual deaths, and municipal paperwork turn the graveyard into a darkly funny test of whether the dead are counted or truly seen.

items.title: Diggers — 2011 Edition
items.description: A retired gravedigger digs his own grave each night and fills it each morning. When his son returns carrying a new name, father and child collide over inheritance, loss, and who has the right to define a life. Gretchen's silent perspective complicates what either man thinks he knows.

items.title: re(Fill)
items.description: Two nonfiction essays probe the ways time and treatment alter a family. In 90PLUS HIGH, a grandfather's hip surgery leads to questions about opioid prescriptions, dependence, and extreme old age; TIME IS ALL WE ASK FOR confronts mourning through the sound and limits of elegy.

items.title: The Stage Plays: Monet Marcel by Delray
Diggers — 2011 Edition (archive copy)
items.description: Archive edition of Diggers: a gravedigger's daily ritual of opening and closing a grave frames a family struggle over grief, a son's chosen name, and the claims of the past. The play brings housing bureaucracy and intimacy into the same backyard.

items.title: Clwns Bund
items.description: In Hollow Wood, DangR's role as Teller turns objects into evidence of what people survived. Tooth-clerks, beetle indexers, and rules governing 'authorized whimsy' make this unsettling tale an inquiry into childhood, mass violence, witness, and the price of memory.

items.title: Just Give Me Water
items.description: A glass of water becomes the object of a twenty-year absence in these raw, broken-voice poems. Repetition and abrupt confession move between grief, the impulse to stay upright, and the first recollection of heroin use.

items.title: 35 Years Old
items.description: The poems of Thirty Five Years Old grow from phone notes, unsent messages, and the exhaustion of wanting closeness while distrusting it. Fragmented lines trace addiction's shadow, queer invisibility, and the long work of speaking without self-editing.

items.title: Humidor Lecture 1
items.description: First lecture, presented as a flipbook.

items.title: SHIVA — Theatrical Edition
items.description: A theatrical edition from the MDNT MRKT archive.

items.title: SHIVA / 7DYSWTSE
items.description: The companion publication in the SHIVA sequence.

items.title: Calder City, Michigan
items.description: Nine linked stories map the west side of Grand Rapids through the eyes of Dangr Mouse, a witness who stays rather than leaves. A laundromat, church, and neighborhood bulletin board hold the distinct lives of residents whose memory makes a community.

items.title: The Humidor — Lecture 2
items.description: In the second Humidor lecture, brining and a smoker's drying rack become models for creative distribution. Salt, sugar, and water stand beside time, platform, and audience as the essay studies the interval between publishing work and making it resonate.

items.title: Once: On Poetic Form
items.description: An inquiry into poetic form.

items.title: almasexual
items.description: A collection of Delray poems written across 2010–2026, including sonnets that turn ordinary cloth, a sister's care, teaching, and household labor into records of lives official history neglects. Intimacy and social structure share the same line.

items.title: DSMSSED CLWNS
items.description: An entry in the CLWNS experimental cycle.

items.title: Cornbread
items.description: A work from the MDNT MRKT literary catalog.

items.title: SMKSTACK WHITEPAGES
items.description: White papers and working material from SMKSTACK.

items.title: NOTES on Decline — Play
items.description: In Hollow Wood, a sentient mirror named Care becomes both witness and captive. Across interrogations separated by centuries, DangR, Heron Halo, and investigators confront creation, identity, punishment, and an apology whose words have been withheld too long.

items.title: CLWNTWN
items.description: An installment of the CLWNTWN universe.

items.title: CLOWN BOUND
items.description: In Hollow Wood, DangR measures the histories lodged in common things while clerks and elaborate rules try to contain the aftermath of catastrophe. A bent spoon may be scrap or inheritance depending on who remembers it, and the teller must decide what counts as value.

items.title: VoyeurS — A Novella
items.description: A novella from the MDNT MRKT literary archive.

items.title: MarrowOps
items.description: Under refinery light in Delray, DangR waits for a coded signal and meets Mous3 for an operation aimed at the city's hidden marrow. Shifting voices, surveillance, and uncanny returns bring questions of identity and control into an industrial night.

items.title: Journal
items.description: A journal from the MDNT MRKT archive.

items.title: In the midst of DangR
items.description: Two men fleeing the law take shelter in a haunted Grand Rapids rectory. As Mouse and Cornbread encounter a presence that witnesses more than it threatens, the novel turns inherited debt, guilt, and the grammar of what has already happened into a theory of haunting.
